learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to calculate the behavior of systems and determine their parameters based on measured system responses.
They can evaluate measurement errors and, if necessary, perform correction calculations.
They also know how physical measurement signals are converted, processed, and evaluated, and what display devices exist and how they are operated.
Furthermore, they know the most important measurement methods in mechanical engineering and can apply them appropriately.

syllabus_topics: Introduction (basic concepts, standards, examples, goals of the lecture)
Fundamentals of system description and analysis (differential equations and their solution using Laplace transformation, characteristic value determination based on step response, frequency response)
Measurement errors (causes, types of errors, normal distribution, error propagation)
Components of (analog) measuring chains (transducer elements, bridge and amplifier circuits, multimeters, oscilloscopes)
Measurement methods (e.g., using strain gauges, for temperature, displacement/position)
assessment_rules: To receive credit points, the module examination must be passed and proof of performance (active participation in the practical course, consisting of 3 experiments) must be provided. The value of the grade for the final grade is according to the SPO.
